title: Feelings and opinions
description: Say how you feel, what you like and dislike, what you think, and whether you agree.

guide.title: Two ways to have a feeling
guide.text:
Some feelings are adjectives used with 'I am', as in English: मैं खुश हूँ (khush, happy), मैं परेशान हूँ (pareshaan, worried, bothered), मैं उदास हूँ (udaas, sad), मैं थका हुआ हूँ (tired). Adjectives such as खुश, परेशान and उदास do not change for gender.

Many others are nouns that come to you, strike you or happen to you, in the 'to me' pattern:

डर लगना (dar lagnaa): fear strikes. मुझे डर लग रहा है, 'I am scared'.
गुस्सा आना (gussaa aanaa): anger comes. मुझे गुस्सा आ रहा है, 'I am getting angry'.
दुख होना (dukh honaa): sorrow happens. मुझे दुख हुआ, 'I was saddened'.
खुशी होना (khushee honaa): happiness happens. मुझे बहुत खुशी हुई, 'I was very glad'.
याद आना (yaad aanaa): memory comes. मुझे आपकी याद आती है, 'I miss you', literally 'your memory comes to me'.

In these sentences the verb agrees with the feeling: डर and गुस्सा are masculine (लग रहा है, आ रहा है); खुशी and याद are feminine (हुई, आती है).

guide.title: Liking: three shades
guide.text:
पसंद है (pasand hai) states a standing preference: मुझे संगीत बहुत पसंद है, 'I like music very much'.

पसंद आया (pasand aayaa), 'came to be liked', is your reaction to something you have just tried: मुझे खाना पसंद आया, 'I liked the food'.

अच्छा लगना (achchhaa lagnaa), 'to feel good, to seem good', is the warmest and commonest: मुझे बहुत अच्छा लगा, 'I liked it a lot', 'that felt really nice'. Here अच्छा agrees with the thing liked: यह फ़िल्म मुझे अच्छी लगी.

To ask someone's reaction: आपको कैसा लगा? 'How did you like it?' To ask how they are feeling right now: आपको कैसा लग रहा है?

guide.title: Giving an opinion
guide.text:
'I think' is usually मुझे लगता है (mujhe lagtaa hai), 'it seems to me', followed by what you think. The linking word कि (ki, 'that') may be included or left out: मुझे लगता है (कि) आप सही हैं, 'I think you are right'.

Other openers: मेरे विचार से (mere vichaar se), 'in my opinion', and शायद (shaayad), 'perhaps'.

सही (sahee) is 'right, correct' and गलत (galat) is 'wrong'. To agree: मैं आपसे सहमत हूँ (sahmat), 'I agree with you', or more simply आप ठीक कह रहे हैं, 'you are right in what you say', or just हाँ, बिलकुल. To disagree gently: मुझे ऐसा नहीं लगता, 'I don't think so', literally 'it does not seem so to me'.

Describing things: मज़ेदार (mazedaar) is 'fun, enjoyable, tasty', बढ़िया (barhiyaa) is 'great', बेकार (bekaar) is 'useless, rubbish'.

examples.native: मुझे लगता है आप सही हैं।
examples.roman: mujhe lagtaa hai aap sahee hain.

guide.title: Reassuring someone
guide.text:
चिंता (chintaa) is 'worry'. चिंता मत कीजिए is 'don't worry', and चिंता की कोई बात नहीं is 'there is nothing to worry about', literally 'there is no matter of worry'. The pattern X की कोई बात नहीं is productive: डर की कोई बात नहीं, 'there is nothing to be afraid of'.

सब ठीक हो जाएगा, 'everything will be fine', is what you say next.

examples.english: There is nothing to worry about.
There is nothing to be afraid of.

phrases.note: The same for men and women: परेशान does not change, and थोड़ा is an adverb here. Many women also say मैं थोड़ी परेशान हूँ (main thoree pareshaan hoon).
Said on hearing bad news, like 'I am sorry to hear that'.

phrases.native: मुझे लगता है आप सही हैं।
phrases.roman: mujhe lagtaa hai aap sahee hain.
phrases.literal: to-me seems is you right are

phrases.note: Rather formal. In conversation people say आप ठीक कह रहे हैं (aap theek kah rahe hain), 'you are right'.
